newsitem.title: USA: Sun trims costs but seen with much to do.
newsitem.headline: Sun trims costs but seen with much to do.

text.p: Sun Co Inc's exit from the American Petroleum Institute (API) is a another small step in its drive to trim costs, but there is still a lot of cutting left to do, analysts said.
Sun, which announced the pullout on Tuesday, said the move will save it more than $2 million each year in dues and help it compete more effectively in the cutthroat refining and marketing sector.
But the company's shares continue to lag badly behind the market, despite a little boost after the announcement earlier this week that Shell Oil Co, Texaco Inc and Star (Texaco's joint
venture with state-owned Saudi Aramco) were in talks to merge their downstream operations.
"They've lagged the industry in terms of cutting costs," said James Falvey, analyst at Smith Barney in Boston. "It's a very small step in the right direction (but) there's still a lot Sun can do."
Sun said it will stay in the National Petroleum Refiners Association (NPRA), which is considered by many to be more attuned to companies concetrated in the downstream sector.
Analysts said Sun badly needs to focus on running a tighter ship to better compete with other independent refining and marketing companies, such as Tosco Corp.

Having reached $68 in the late 1980s, Sun's shares have badly trailed the Dow Jones Industrial index in the past five years. Morgan Stanley downgraded Sun in August for failing to implement a cost-cutting program and with depressed industry margins the shares hit $22 in early September, their lowest in more than a decade. They ended Wednesday up 1/8 at $24 1/4.
"They've consistently disappointed the Street," Falvey said,
referring the investment community's impression of Sun. "But they've got hope," he said.

He noted Sun could save a lot of money by cutting jobs, streamlining procurement and in particular, improving the running of the 195,000 barrel per day (bpd) Girard Point portion of its 315,000 bpd Philadelphia refining complex.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
